oracle.description: This JSON file is the single normative authority for action approval. The design, decisions, and coverage Markdown files are checked views. If a view or downstream implementation conflicts with this file, this file wins.
oracle.scope: Independent human-present approval for a frozen local action plan, followed by one atomic consume-and-claim by a distinct unattended agent principal.
oracle.compatibilityRule: No /v1 caller, credential, scope string, authorization ID, prompt, or legacy proposal can stand in for an action-approval-authority-v1 artifact. A field, profile, seal, state, transition, or verification-rule change requires a new oracle digest and renewed review.

productDecision.source: interactive user decision received 2026-08-18 after the SEC-R02-DESIGN stop
productDecision.text: After a human-present operator verifies the frozen preview, that operator may seal an expiring one-use approval. A distinct unattended agent principal may later atomically consume it and commit.
fixedConsequences: A creator may be an operator-interactive or agent-unattended principal when its authenticated profile grants mail:action.create.
Only an operator-interactive authenticated profile with fresh request-bound human-presence evidence may approve.
Only an agent-unattended authenticated profile with mail:action.commit may consume and commit.
The committer principal ID and credential ID must both differ from the approver principal ID and credential ID.
The executor is an internal daemon capability, never a public principal or bearer profile.
Principal, credential, profile, scopes, authentication lifetime, and user presence come only from the authenticator.
No credential profile may contain both approval and unattended commit authority; scope-only or caller-supplied identity evidence fails closed.

authenticatorDecision.source: interactive user decision received after the root-review authenticator stop
authenticatorDecision.text: Use a macOS Keychain/Secure Enclave P-256 credential protected by device-owner user presence, with daemon-issued single-use request-bound challenges, a native CLI broker, and daemon public-key verification.
authenticatorDecision.fallback: fail-closed; unsupported hardware or unavailable device-owner authentication cannot approve or cancel

terms.name: FrozenActionPlan
terms.meaning: Server-owned immutable action kind, ordered target set, preconditions, creation time, plan expiry, version, canonical preview bytes, and preview digest.

terms.name: Creator
terms.meaning: The authenticated operator-interactive or agent-unattended principal that created the frozen plan. Creation grants no approval authority.

terms.name: Approver
terms.meaning: The authenticated human-present operator-interactive principal that reviewed the exact frozen preview and sealed its approval.

terms.name: Committer
terms.meaning: The authenticated agent-unattended principal that atomically consumes an available approval and claims its exact plan.

terms.name: Executor
terms.meaning: The internal daemon action-executor-v1 capability that receives only a durable claim and consumption receipt; it has no public credential or scope.

terms.name: ApprovalArtifact
terms.meaning: An immutable, HMAC-sealed, expiring authority record for exactly one plan version, preview, target set, normalized intent, and mail:action.commit scope.

terms.name: ConsumptionReceipt
terms.meaning: The immutable durable proof that one committer consumed one approval in the same transaction that created the plan claim.

terms.name: HumanPresence
terms.meaning: A fresh request-bound assertion verified by the authenticator from a non-exportable operator credential; a prompt, TTY, request field, or static bearer token is not human presence.

profiles.credential: A1 macOS Secure Enclave P-256 credential using kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly plus SecAccessControl userPresence/privateKeyUsage, fresh zero-reuse LAContext signing, and daemon request-bound challenge verification. Static bearer credentials are forbidden.
profiles.nonApprovalSession: An A1-minted memory-only operator session may authenticate only mail:action.create and mail:action.inspect for at most 600 seconds and never carries mail:action.approve or mail:action.commit.

profiles.credential: Exportable or machine-held credential resolved only to this profile; it carries no approval capability.
No public credential. The executor accepts only an internal capability carrying an already durable plan claim and consumption receipt.

authorityMatrix.durableOutput: operator_presence_challenge_consumptions plus action_approvals in one transaction
operator_presence_challenge_consumptions plus action_approval_cancellations and plan version update in one transaction
action_approval_consumptions plus action_plan_claims in one transaction

structurallyForbidden.rule: Configuration and authenticator construction reject every credential containing mail:action.approve or retired mail:action.authorize together with mail:action.commit.
operator-interactive rejects mail:action.commit even when the scope appears in credential material.
agent-unattended rejects mail:action.approve and mail:action.authorize even when either scope appears in credential material.
One credential ID resolves to exactly one profile. Duplicate credential IDs, profile unions, fallback profiles, and profile inference from requested scopes fail daemon startup.

A static bearer or file token cannot resolve to operator-interactive. Only a memory-only A1-minted non-approval session may use Bearer authentication for operator create/inspect, and it is structurally incapable of approve or commit.

An operator session has the exact closed scope set mail:action.create plus mail:action.inspect and is rejected for approve, cancel, commit, executor, challenge administration, credential administration, and seal-key administration.
Consume rejects when committer principal ID equals approver principal ID, committer credential ID equals approver credential ID, or committer profile is not agent-unattended.
No operation registry entry, HTTP route, CLI command, scope, or credential exposes internal-action-executor.
Strict public schemas contain no principalId, credentialId, profile, scopes, userPresence, executor identity, issuedAt, expiresAt, nonce, authorizationScope, seal key ID, or seal value input field.

verification: All context fields are decoded from unknown, bounded, frozen, and passed out-of-band to the service; request JSON cannot override them.

Operator create and inspect require a current A1-minted non-approval session whose exact scopes are mail:action.create and mail:action.inspect; the session cannot authenticate approve, cancel, commit, or executor operations.

Approve and cancel require a non-exportable operator signing credential and an authenticator-verified user-presence assertion bound to the exact HTTP method, concrete route, and SHA-256 of the final bounded raw request-body bytes.

After EOF and strict boundary parsing, the approval service independently reconstructs the expected method and concrete path, recomputes SHA-256 from the retained final bounded raw request-body bytes, and compares all three against the authenticated presence context before any authority write.

At approval or cancellation time, verifiedAt is no more than 60 seconds old, the operation time is before validUntil plus at most 5 seconds accepted clock skew, and ceremonyId has not authorized any earlier approval operation. Ceremony uniqueness spans approve and cancel.
Commit authentication must be current at consume time. Approver and committer credential records must not be revoked; unavailable credential status fails closed.

operatorRequestBindings.cliBodyEncoding: JSON.stringify({planId,planVersion,previewDigest}) encoded as UTF-8 once and retained unchanged
operatorRequestBindings.bodySha256: lowercaseHex(SHA-256(final bounded raw HTTP body bytes)); the CLI bytes equal cliBodyEncoding, and any other accepted client must challenge and transmit the same exact strict JSON bytes

operatorRequestBindings.cliBodyEncoding: JSON.stringify({planId,approvalId,planVersion,previewDigest}) encoded as UTF-8 once and retained unchanged
operatorRequestBindings.bodySha256: lowercaseHex(SHA-256(final bounded raw HTTP body bytes)); the CLI bytes equal cliBodyEncoding, and any other accepted client must challenge and transmit the same exact strict JSON bytes

operatorAuthenticatorProtocol.platform: macOS with Secure Enclave and Security.framework device-owner user presence
operatorAuthenticatorProtocol.availabilityPolicy: Secure Enclave is mandatory. If key generation, device-owner authentication, or the native broker is unavailable, approval, cancellation, and seal-key administration fail with action.operator_presence_unsupported. There is no software-key, passphrase, static-bearer, prompt-only, remote-header, agent-token, or same-UID-only fallback.

key.privateKey: Generated by the native broker using kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom, 256 bits, kSecAttrTokenIDSecureEnclave, kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly, and SecAccessControl userPresence plus privateKeyUsage. Private key bytes are never exportable. Missing or removed device credentials fail closed and no weaker accessibility class is accepted.
key.publicKeyEncoding: DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo for id-ecPublicKey plus prime256v1; base64url without padding in configuration
key.signatureEncoding: 64-byte IEEE-P1363 r||s, normalized to low-S by the broker, base64url without padding; daemon rejects non-low-S, zero, out-of-range, wrong-length, DER, padded, or non-canonical encodings
key.verification: Daemon resolves the active credential record, decodes its SPKI, verifies P-256/SHA-256 over exact assertionCommitment UTF-8 bytes, and only then treats the record's principal/profile as authenticated.
key.authenticationContext: The broker creates a fresh LAContext for every signature, sets touchIDAuthenticationAllowableReuseDuration to 0, supplies it only to that SecKey signing call, and discards it after success/failure. No authenticated context or biometric success is cached between challenges.

instance.authorityInstanceId: instance:<UUIDv4 lowercase canonical text>, generated once during daemon configuration and stored outside the database
instance.purpose: Binds enrollment and challenges to this daemon installation so a signed assertion cannot move between installations.

enrollment.broker: A native executable named agent-mail-operator-broker linked to Security.framework; #204 owns it and its narrow daemon provisioning adapter.
commandRules: Commands accept no principal, profile, scope, key material, assertion, or presence flags. privateRoot is the existing canonical startup root and never appears in the stored commitment.

Every command requires an attached TTY, takes the owner-only configuration/admission lock, verifies the caller effective UID equals the privateRoot owner, and exposes no JSON/noninteractive/yes/environment bypass.

enroll is allowed only when no active operator credential exists. rotate requires a signed fresh-presence rotation commitment from the current active key and a separately signed enrollment commitment from the new key while authority admission is locked; it atomically writes the new active/old revoked configuration first, then invalidates every old-key available challenge and unconsumed approval before releasing admission.

revoke requires a fresh-presence revocation commitment from that active credential while authority admission is locked. It atomically marks the configuration record revoked first, then invalidates all of its available challenges and unconsumed approvals in one database transaction before releasing admission. A crash between writes is fail-closed because the durable configuration already makes the credential inactive; startup completes invalidation before admission.

recover is the only path when no enrolled private key can sign. It requires fresh Security.framework deviceOwnerAuthentication on an attached TTY and a newly signed enrollment commitment for a new authorityInstanceId. While admission is locked it atomically writes the new instance/new active key/all old keys revoked first, then invalidates every available challenge and unconsumed approval regardless of credential/key before releasing admission. It never preserves live authority.
enrollment.enrollmentId: enrollment:<UUIDv4 lowercase canonical text>, generated by the broker before key creation
enrollment.enrollmentCommitment: JSON.stringify(["agent-mail-operator-enrollment-v1", authorityInstanceId, enrollmentId, principalId, credentialId, "operator-interactive", "ES256", publicKeySpkiBase64url, enrolledAt, enrollmentNonceBase64url])

administrationCommitments.rotate: JSON.stringify(["agent-mail-operator-rotation-v1", authorityInstanceId, currentCredentialId, replacementCredentialId, replacementPublicKeySpkiSha256, requestedAt, administrationNonceBase64url]) signed by the current key; the replacement separately signs its enrollmentCommitment
administrationCommitments.revoke: JSON.stringify(["agent-mail-operator-revocation-v1", authorityInstanceId, credentialId, requestedAt, administrationNonceBase64url]) signed by the credential being revoked
administrationCommitments.nonceAndTime: administrationNonceBase64url is 32 cryptographically random bytes encoded without padding; requestedAt is the daemon canonical millisecond UTC clock and the signed administration request expires after 60 seconds

localizedReasons.rotateCurrent: Agent Mail ROTATE current operator key
localizedReasons.rotateReplacement: Agent Mail ENROLL replacement operator key
localizedReasons.recoverReplacement: Agent Mail ENROLL recovered operator key

procedure: The local provisioning command requires an attached TTY, generates a 32-byte random enrollment nonce, displays the fixed operator principal and key fingerprint, and asks the OS for device-owner presence with an enrollment-specific reason.
The Secure Enclave key signs the exact enrollment commitment. The broker immediately verifies the signature with the exported public key.
The daemon provisioning adapter, under an owner-only configuration lock, validates the commitment/signature and atomically writes the public credential record; it never receives private key material.

A credential record is active only after a successful signed enrollment. Caller-supplied principal/profile values are not accepted; v1 uses the fixed principal:local-operator and operator-interactive profile.

configurationRecord.writeRule: Decode strict JSON, require the privateRoot owner UID, hold the configuration/admission lock, write a same-directory 0600 temporary file, fsync it, rename atomically, fsync the owner-only directory, then complete required database invalidations before admission resumes.
strictFields: configurationRevision positive integer incremented exactly once per successful mutation

credentialLifetime.rule: Enrollment, rotation, and recovery set expiresAt to enrolledAt plus exactly 365 days using the daemon clock. A credential is current only while now < expiresAt; equality is expired. Expiry cannot be extended in place and immediately blocks challenges, sessions, approve, cancel, and consume validation of approvals signed by that credential.
credentialLifetime.rotation: Rotation creates a replacement with its own new 365-day lifetime. An expired credential cannot sign rotation; recover is required and invalidates all live authority. No omitted, null, sentinel, or infinite expiry is accepted.

nonApprovalOperatorSession.purpose: Authenticate operator-interactive create and inspect without reusing an approval ceremony or requiring presence for every read.

createRoute.exposure: loopback listener only; absent from Tailscale and the agent operation registry
createRoute.authentication: A fresh A1 open-session challenge bound to exact POST/path/raw body; no existing bearer is accepted

challenge.displayCode: Format the first 20 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(JSON.stringify(['agent-mail-presence-display-v1','open-session',authorityInstanceId,'mail:action.create','mail:action.inspect'])) as five groups of four.
challenge.localizedReason: Agent Mail START 10-minute CREATE and INSPECT session
challenge.atomicClosure: Consume the challenge in BEGIN IMMEDIATE with authorityOutputKind operator-session and a daemon-created sessionId; only after commit install the token digest in memory and return the token. Crash before installation/response consumes the ceremony but creates no usable session.

token.wire: base64url without padding in Authorization: Bearer <token>
token.storage: Only SHA-256(token bytes), sessionId, principalId, credentialId, exact two-scope set, sessionAuthEventId, issuedAt, expiresAt, authorityInstanceId, and configurationRevision exist in daemon memory. Token bytes are never written to disk, argv, environment, logs, audit, errors, or structured output.
token.expiry: min(issuedAt plus 600 seconds, credentialExpiresAt); equality is expired
token.restart: All sessions disappear on ordinary restart, explicit restore, configuration revision change, credential revocation/expiry/rotation, or authority instance recovery.
token.authorization: Bearer resolution from unknown must find the exact digest, active credential, matching authority instance/configuration revision, now before session and credential expiry, and exact scopes. The resulting profile is operator-interactive with presence kind a1-non-approval-session. Any approval/commit scope or operation rejects before body read.

challenge.issueTransport: Owner-local broker RPC, not a public operation-registry route and not reachable through Tailscale. The daemon exposes it only on an owner-only 0600 Unix-domain socket under the configured runtime directory.
challenge.issueFraming: One request per connection: canonical UTF-8 JSON followed by exactly one LF byte and then write-half close. The complete frame, including LF, is capped at 4096 bytes; CR, additional lines, trailing bytes, invalid UTF-8, missing LF, or a second request rejects. The daemon returns one canonical UTF-8 JSON line and closes. The socket parent is mode 0700, the socket is mode 0600, and getpeereid must equal the daemon/privateRoot owner UID.

issueRequest.requestBodyBase64url: Canonical base64url without padding of the exact final raw UTF-8 HTTP or owner-local administration body bytes the broker will later transmit; decoded bytes are capped at 2048 and retained unchanged for the final request

challenge.nonce: 32 cryptographically random bytes, base64url without padding
challenge.operatorDisplayCode: For approve/cancel, format the first 20 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(JSON.stringify(["agent-mail-presence-display-v1", operation, planId, planVersion, previewDigest])) as five groups of four separated by hyphens. For open-session, use nonApprovalOperatorSession.challenge.displayCode. For seal-key administration, use approvalSealKeyring.administrationProtocol.displayCode.
challenge.errorResponse: JSON.stringify({version:'agent-mail-macos-operator-presence-v1',error:{code,message}}) plus LF; code/message exactly reuse the matching public action.operator_presence_unsupported, action.operator_challenge_capacity, action.operator_assertion_invalid, or action.approval_forbidden entry and expose no path, key, signature, or biometric detail
issuanceRules: The owner-only RPC validates its 4096-byte envelope and 2048-byte decoded-body caps before JSON parsing, decodes the strict request and final raw body, parses that body with the target HTTP or administration operation's strict schema, resolves one active operator credential, and independently reconstructs the exact method/path/body SHA-256/display code.
Challenge principal/profile/instance/times/nonce come from daemon state, never the RPC request.
Expired available challenges are durably closed before capacity is counted. Capacity or rate overflow returns a bounded error and creates no challenge.
Challenge rows are immutable. One challenge is available, consumed, expired, or invalidated and can never return to available.

assertion.assertionCommitment: The exact stored challenge commitment bytes; no client-selected field is appended.
assertion.humanConfirmation: Before signing, the CLI renders the full plan/preview or exact seal-key administration target plus operatorDisplayCode. Approval/cancellation localizedReason is exactly 'Agent Mail <APPROVE|CANCEL> plan <planId> preview <previewDigest> code <operatorDisplayCode>'. Seal-key administration uses approvalSealKeyring.administrationProtocol.localizedReasons. The user compares the same target and code in CLI and OS prompt.
verificationOrder: Before reading the body, bounded admission parses only the <=2048-byte assertion envelope, resolves an available unexpired challenge and active credential, and checks expected method and concrete path. This is provisional admission, not an authenticated principal.

The HTTP boundary then reads at most the registered operation byte limit, updates SHA-256 incrementally for every raw body byte, and only after EOF parses the already bounded bytes with the strict operation schema.
The authority service independently reconstructs the exact operation method/path and compares the streamed raw-body digest with both the stored challenge and verified assertion context.

The daemon verifies the canonical low-S P1363 signature over the exact stored challenge commitment, checks instance/credential/profile/time/revocation, and constructs operator-interactive context only from the credential and challenge rows.

For public HTTP, challenge consumption and operator-session output ID, approval insertion, or cancellation closure/version update occur in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. For seal-key administration, the exact exclusive-lock procedure in approvalSealKeyring.administrationProtocol consumes the challenge and records the resulting keyring revision. Signature success without completed mutation grants no authority.

Any mismatch, malformed signature, expired/revoked record, stale configuration/keyring revision, reused ceremony, transaction race, trailing body byte, alternate JSON whitespace, body reserialization, or same-UID request without a current assertion fails closed with no session/approval/cancellation/administration authority.

lifecycle.ordinaryRestart: Available challenges and approvals may survive an ordinary restart only until their original expiry and only with the same authority instance and active unexpired credential/key configuration. Memory-only operator sessions never survive restart.
lifecycle.revocation: Revoking or expiring a credential clears its memory-only sessions and atomically invalidates its available challenges and unconsumed approvals with one exact plan-version advance per affected still-pending plan before new admission. Consumed receipts remain audit facts.
lifecycle.rotation: At most two active operator credentials may coexist. Enroll and verify the replacement first, mark replacedByCredentialId, then revoke the old credential; outstanding old-key challenges/approvals invalidate on revocation.
lifecycle.databaseRestore: Every explicit database restore invalidates every restored available challenge and every restored unconsumed approval before service admission, regardless of whether the old credential, Secure Enclave private key, approval HMAC key, or matching config is still present.
lifecycle.machineRecovery: ThisDeviceOnly private keys do not migrate. A replacement Mac requires fresh enrollment and invalidates all restored live authority; there is no key export or recovery bypass.

format.keyringRevision: positive safe integer incremented exactly once per successful mutation
format.activeKeyId: approval-seal-key:<UUIDv4 lowercase canonical text> naming exactly one active entry
format.keyBase64url: exactly 32 cryptographically random bytes encoded canonical base64url without padding
format.ordering: keys sorted ascending by bytewise UTF-8 keyId; exactly one active key; no duplicate IDs or key bytes

approvalSealKeyring.generation: On first configured startup with no database and no keyring, generate one 32-byte key with the operating-system CSPRNG and one UUIDv4 key ID. A missing keyring beside an existing database is never regenerated and blocks authority admission.
approvalSealKeyring.writeRule: Under the exclusive authority configuration locks, write a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and no symlink following, fsync the file, rename atomically, fsync the mode-0700 directory, reload/strictly validate, then complete required database invalidations before releasing admission.
approvalSealKeyring.rotation: Rotation adds a new CSPRNG key as the only active key and changes the prior active key to verify-only in one atomic file replacement. New approvals use only the new key; existing approvals continue to verify with their referenced verify-only key and remain consumable.
approvalSealKeyring.removal: Removal is allowed only for a verify-only key. While admission is exclusively locked, atomically remove it from the keyring first, then invalidate every unconsumed approval referencing it and advance each still-pending plan version exactly once in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Startup performs the same invalidation if a referenced key is missing. Active-key removal is rejected; rotate first.
approvalSealKeyring.validation: Every load rejects unknown fields, malformed/canonicality failures, wrong mode/owner/type, symlinks, revision regression, zero/multiple active keys, invalid IDs/status/time, wrong key length, or duplicate IDs/bytes. A seal mismatch or missing referenced key never falls back to another key.
approvalSealKeyring.backupExclusion: The keyring path is categorically excluded from database backup inputs, backup manifests, restore payloads, diagnostic bundles, logs, errors, and telemetry. Backup verification fails if any keyring path, key ID-to-bytes mapping, key bytes, or operator credential private material is present.

administrationProtocol.purpose: Make seal-key rotation/removal depend on daemon-verifiable fresh A1 presence rather than trusting a same-UID process or a client-side prompt.

seal-key-rotate.encoding: JSON.stringify({expectedKeyringRevision,expectedActiveKeyId}) once as UTF-8; values come from the daemon's current keyring challenge response

seal-key-remove.encoding: JSON.stringify({expectedKeyringRevision,keyId}) once as UTF-8; keyId must name an existing verify-only key

administrationProtocol.displayCode: Format the first 20 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(JSON.stringify(['agent-mail-presence-display-v1',operation,authorityInstanceId,expectedKeyringRevision,targetKeyId])) as five groups of four; targetKeyId is expectedActiveKeyId for rotate and keyId for remove.

localizedReasons.seal-key-rotate: Agent Mail ROTATE approval seal key <expectedActiveKeyId> revision <expectedKeyringRevision> code <operatorDisplayCode>
localizedReasons.seal-key-remove: Agent Mail REMOVE approval seal key <keyId> revision <expectedKeyringRevision> code <operatorDisplayCode>

administrationProtocol.mutationTransport: The existing owner-only daemon mutation UDS remains non-public. One strict canonical JSON line has fields in order version, requestBodyBase64url, assertion; version is agent-mail-action-authority-admin-v1, body is the identical retained bytes, and assertion is the exact A1 assertion object. Frame/LF/UID/owner/mode/4096-byte limits match the challenge RPC. Same UID is transport admission only and never authority.
administrationProtocol.verification: The daemon rejects the old bare rotate/remove discriminants. It decodes the bounded body from unknown, resolves the available challenge, requires operation plus ADMIN plus exact internal path plus raw-body SHA-256, verifies the current active unexpired operator credential and low-S P-256 assertion over the stored challenge commitment, and rechecks authority instance, operator configuration revision, keyring revision, active/target key status, and display code under the exclusive authority locks.
administrationProtocol.atomicMutation: After verification and while retaining the exclusive file/process locks, replace and fsync the keyring, then in BEGIN IMMEDIATE consume the challenge with authorityOutputKind seal-key-rotation or seal-key-removal and authorityOutputId seal-keyring-revision:<newRevision>, perform removal invalidations/version advances, commit, reload, and release. Rotate creates exactly one new active key; remove accepts only the challenged verify-only key. Active/missing removal rejects without consuming the challenge or changing files/DB.
administrationProtocol.crashAndReplay: The challenge body binds expectedKeyringRevision. If a crash occurs after the file replacement but before challenge consumption, the file's n+1 revision makes the still-available n challenge unusable; startup under exclusive locks durably invalidates that stale challenge and completes required DB invalidations before admission. A completed challenge cannot rotate/remove twice, and assertion/body/method/path/target/revision mutation rejects.
administrationProtocol.cliRules: The broker command requires attached TTY, shows operation, exact key target/revision, and display code, asks y/yes with fail-closed EOF/non-TTY rules, then uses a fresh zero-reuse LAContext to sign. No --yes, --force, environment, stdin, saved assertion, operator session, agent credential, software key, prompt-only, or unattended fallback exists.

approvalSealKeyring.authorization: Both commands require the exact daemon-issued single-use A1 administration challenge and assertion in administrationProtocol. Attached TTY and same UID are necessary but insufficient; the daemon verifies fresh Secure Enclave presence, exact operation/target/revision/body, and challenge consumption under the exclusive authority locks.

authorityLinearization.lockFile: <privateRoot>/runtime/action-authority.lock, regular owner-owned mode-0600 file opened without symlink following
order: Acquire advisory flock shared for approve/cancel/consume/session authentication, exclusive for credential/key mutation, recovery, and explicit restore.
Acquire the matching in-process authority configuration read/write lock.
Read and strictly validate operator configuration revision, authorityInstanceId, credential record/expiry, seal keyring revision, active/reference keys, and file identity/digests.
Open SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE only after both locks; no code may acquire these resources in another order.
Immediately before commit, re-read the in-memory revisions and file identity/digests under the same locks; mismatch rolls back and returns no authority/capability.

For consume, commit the receipt/claim/plan update, construct and return the executor capability, and only then release the read locks. For configuration mutation, atomically replace the outside-DB file first, perform all DB closures/version/state changes, commit, reload memory, and only then release exclusive locks.
authorityLinearization.linearizationRule: If consume holds the shared locks first, it commits and returns its executor capability before revocation/key removal can linearize. If an exclusive mutation holds first, it makes the outside-DB authority unusable, closes affected database authority, and releases before consume can validate; the later consume rejects. No ordering allows mutation to linearize first and a later consume to return a capability.
authorityLinearization.crashRule: A crash after an outside-DB atomic replacement but before database closure is fail-closed. Startup takes exclusive locks and completes invalidations/version advances/quarantine from the stricter current files before listeners, session resolution, recovery, or challenge RPC start.

trustedFieldSources.source: authenticated create context: exact A1 non-approval operator session or agent-unattended credential
active A1 credential record, consumed open-session challenge, daemon clock/configuration, and memory-only token digest record
trustedFieldSources.callerMaySupply: only the opaque token is presented; every authority field is server-owned

trustedFieldSources.source: daemon configuration, durable challenge, verified A1 signature, strict target body, and streamed raw-body digest
trustedFieldSources.callerMaySupply: broker transports exact raw bytes and signature, but the service independently derives and verifies every trusted value

trustedFieldSources.source: daemon internal capability and process incarnation
server-created namespaced UUID and stored plan
trustedFieldSources.callerMaySupply: echo-only on approve and commit; exact path/body/store match required
echo-only; exact match and recomputation required

trustedFieldSources.source: server canonicalization of stored action kind and target digest
minimum of plan expiry, credential expiry, and issuedAt plus 600 seconds
strict owner-only operator configuration and seal keyring under authority locks

trustedFieldSources.callerMaySupply: approvalId is echo-only on commit; others never supplied

trustedFieldSources.source: daemon clock inside the closure transaction

canonicalization.encoding: UTF-8 JSON arrays with no whitespace; strings are existing strict NFC-safe identifiers; integers are JSON safe integers; timestamps are canonical millisecond UTC strings
canonicalization.targetOrder: Sort ascending by bytewise UTF-8 comparison of accountId, then mailboxId, then uidValidity numeric, uid numeric, and precondition.modseq numeric.
canonicalization.previewBytes: JSON.stringify(["action-preview-v1", planId, planVersion, action.kind, canonicalTargetSet, normalizedIntent, createdAt, planExpiresAt])
canonicalization.seal: lowercaseHex(HMAC-SHA-256(key identified by sealKeyId, approvalCommitment UTF-8 bytes))
canonicalization.receiptCommitment: JSON.stringify(["action-approval-consumption-v1", receiptId, approvalId, planId, planVersionBefore, planVersionAfter, claimId, committerPrincipalId, committerCredentialId, committerProfile, committerAuthEventId, consumedAt, approvalCommitmentSha256, executorProfile])

approvalArtifact.sealedFieldProjection: Every immutable field except seal is included exactly once in approvalCommitmentFieldsInOrder; seal is the HMAC output and cannot include itself.
approvalArtifact.expiryRule: expiresAt = min(plan.expiresAt, approver credentialExpiresAt, issuedAt + 600 seconds). If expiresAt <= issuedAt, no approval is issued.
approvalArtifact.availabilityRule: Available means the immutable approval row exists, now < expiresAt, its seal and every recomputed binding match, its approver credential remains recognized and not revoked, and no consumption, expiration, cancellation, or invalidation row exists.
approvalArtifact.multiplicity: At most one approval may be issued for a plan version. A cancelled, expired, or invalidated approval increments the still-pending plan version, forcing a new preview before a replacement approval.

consumptionReceipt.oneUseRule: One approval ID has zero or one consumption receipt. action_approval_consumptions.(plan_id,claim_id) is the sole receipt-to-claim link and a composite foreign key to action_plan_claims; there is no separate link table or nullable evidence field. The receipt insert, claim insert, and pending-to-executing plan version update commit in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.

transitions.guard: active unexpired operator credential; exact two-scope request; valid signed available A1 open-session challenge; current configuration revision
atomicEffects: consume challenge with operator-session output ID
after commit install only token digest and exact bounded session facts in daemon memory

all consume validation succeeds and committer is distinct agent-unattended
atomicEffects: store the receipt row's composite (plan_id,claim_id) foreign key to the inserted claim

transitions.event: clock reaches approval expiry before consume
transitions.planTransition: pending(version n) -> pending(version n+1) unless plan itself expires
atomicEffects: advance the still-pending plan exactly once to version n+1 and regenerate preview bindings, or transition the plan to expired when its own expiry has arrived

transitions.guard: same approver principal; operator-interactive; valid signed available A1 challenge bound to exact DELETE/path/raw body; approval unconsumed

transitions.planTransition: pending(version n) -> pending(version n+1) unless plan is terminal
atomicEffects: advance the still-pending plan exactly once to version n+1 and regenerate preview bindings when possible

set no-new-effect state before any recovery scan

orderedChecks: Decode strict commit request and trusted authenticated context before opening the transaction.
Require agent-unattended profile, exact mail:action.commit scope, current authentication, active credential, and no forbidden scope combination.

While holding the authority shared file/process locks, read plan, proposal, creator, authority-version, approval, closure rows, current operator configuration revision, credential expiry/status, and referenced sealing-key metadata under the SQLite write lock.
If a consumption exists, return action.approval_consumed; if another closure exists, return its stable closure error.
Require plan pending, trusted-v1, exact path/body plan ID, exact plan version, and now before both plan and approval expiry.

Recompute canonical targets, target digest, normalized intent, preview bytes, preview digest, approval commitment, and seal; compare exact bytes in constant time where secrets or digests are compared.

Require approver profile operator-interactive, committer profile agent-unattended, distinct principal IDs, distinct credential IDs, active approver provenance, and exact mail:action.commit artifact scope.

Insert action_plan_claims, insert the consumption receipt whose composite (plan_id,claim_id) foreign key is the sole claim link, and update action_plans pending version n to executing version n+1 with an optimistic WHERE clause.

Recheck outside-DB revisions/file identities, commit, construct and return the internal executor capability containing plan ID, claim ID, receipt ID, plan version after, and executor profile, then release shared authority locks.
atomicConsume.failureRule: Any decode, lookup, scope, profile, provenance, closure, expiry, version, plan, target, intent, digest, seal, or optimistic-update failure rolls back and returns no executor capability and produces zero remote calls.
atomicConsume.concurrencyRule: SQLite write serialization plus unique approval_id on consumption and the plan version update permits exactly one winner. Every loser observes the committed receipt and returns action.approval_consumed.
atomicConsume.replayRule: A second commit never repeats execution and never changes the receipt. It returns HTTP 409 action.approval_consumed with only approvalId, planId, receiptId, and consumedAt.
atomicConsume.cancellationRaceRule: Consume and cancel use BEGIN IMMEDIATE and the same mutually exclusive closure guards. Exactly one closure commits; the loser returns consumed or cancelled and performs no other effect.

restartAndEffects.rule: An available sealed approval survives ordinary daemon restart when its key ID is present and all bindings still verify. Expiry is evaluated before any consume.
Rollback leaves no receipt, claim, or executing plan; the approval remains available if unexpired.

Receipt, claim, and executing plan are durable. Restart resumes through the matching receipt/claim; it cannot consume again and may start only an undispatched target after #202 fresh-authority checks.
Approval remains consumed. Existing uncertain/read-only reconciliation rules apply; no retry may mint or reuse authority.
Every result and terminal attribution remains linked to the original receipt. Partial, failed, expired, rejected, or uncertain outcomes never restore approval availability.
Creator, approver, committer, executor, attempts, receipt, closure, and terminal result reconstruct byte-identically from durable rows.

Every explicit database restore, whether on the same host or another host and whether old credential/HMAC keys remain available or not, atomically invalidates every restored available operator challenge and every restored unconsumed approval. It advances each affected pending plan exactly once. Every restored consumed/executing plan becomes terminal restore-quarantined before recovery with its receipt/claim audit preserved, active claim pointer cleared, version advanced once, and zero executor/resume permission. This prevents pre-consume, pre-cancel, and post-consume/pre-dispatch snapshots from resurrecting effects.
The active key issues approvals; prior keys remain verify-only until every approval they signed is closed or expired. Removing a needed key first invalidates its unconsumed approvals.

storageSchema.placement: After action-result-reconciliation in the dependency-complete action chain; the application registry assigns the next contiguous global schema version.
storageSchema.tablePolicy: All 13 tables are SQLite STRICT tables. Every listed column is NOT NULL, every named primary/unique/foreign/check constraint is enforced with foreign_keys=ON, and no authority table uses delete/update cascades. There are no omitted nullable columns; terminal audit rows exist only for receipt-backed executing, terminal, or restore-quarantined plans.

columns: request_method TEXT CHECK POST|DELETE and operation match
operator_display_code TEXT canonical five groups of four lowercase hex

columns: authority_output_id TEXT namespaced operator-session/approval ID or seal-keyring-revision:<positive safe integer> matching kind
tables.immutability: no update or delete; operation-specific trigger requires the matching operator-session output ID, approval issue, cancellation closure, or completed seal-key administration revision

columns: presence_request_path TEXT exact concrete approve path
operator_display_code TEXT canonical five groups of four lowercase hex

tables.name: action_approval_consumptions
foreignKeys: (plan_id,claim_id) -> action_plan_claims(plan_id,claim_id); this is the sole receipt-to-claim link

tables.name: action_approval_cancellations

operator_display_code TEXT canonical five groups of four lowercase hex

tables.name: action_attempt_authorities
tables.immutability: no update or delete; must exist before adapter permission

tables.name: action_plan_terminal_audit
columns: effect_attempt_count INTEGER >=0 and equal to the exact committed effect-authority projection length
effect_authority_set_digest TEXT 64 lowercase hex; SHA-256 of the exact canonical effect-authority projection

executor_instance_id TEXT: when started, the one actual namespaced effect executor shared by all projected attempts or exact sentinel executor:multiple when the projection contains multiple distinct effect executors; exact sentinel executor:not-started when never-started-after-restore; executor:unknown-after-restore otherwise
finalizer_kind TEXT CHECK effect-executor|ordinary-recovery|restore-admission; audit role only and never mutation authority
finalizer_instance_id TEXT: executor:* for effect-executor; recovery-finalizer:* for ordinary-recovery; exact sentinel finalizer:restore-admission for restore-admission
restore_event_id TEXT restore-event namespace for explicit restore; exact sentinel restore-event:none for normal finalization
foreignKeys: (receipt_id,plan_id,claim_id) -> action_approval_consumptions(receipt_id,plan_id,claim_id); this exact composite key prevents cross-plan or cross-claim terminal attribution

crossTableConstraints: Challenge closure triggers permit exactly one consumption, expiration, or invalidation row. A consumed challenge must match operation, method, path, raw-body digest, active unexpired credential, configuration revision, instance, signature, output kind/ID, and its operator-session/approval/cancellation/seal-key-administration result.

A ceremony ID is the challenge ID and is unique across operator-session issue, approval issue, cancellation, seal-key rotation, and seal-key removal; no challenge may authorize two operations or two authority writes.
Closure insert triggers forbid an approval ID already present in any other consumption, expiration, cancellation, or invalidation table.

Consumption trigger requires approver and committer IDs/profiles to satisfy the exact separation rule; action_approval_consumptions.(plan_id,claim_id) has the sole composite foreign key to action_plan_claims and must match the plan/version/binding rows. No separate receipt-claim link table exists.
Approval trigger requires trusted-v1 plan authority, creator provenance, pending plan, exact plan version, and no earlier approval for that plan version.

Expiration/invalidation/cancellation triggers advance a still-pending matching plan from version n to n+1 exactly once in the same transaction, unless plan expiry transitions it to expired; a closed approval never blocks an approval for the new version.
Attempt-authority trigger requires its receipt, plan, claim, and existing attempt identity to match. restore-quarantined plans reject attempt authority and recovery selection.

The terminal effect-authority projection is JSON.stringify(['action-terminal-effect-authority-set-v1',planId,receiptId,claimId,rows]) where rows contains every exact matching action_attempt_authorities row as [attemptId,executorProfile,executorInstanceId,attributedAt], sorted by UTF-8 attemptId bytes. The terminal count and SHA-256 digest must match that projection. Normal finalization requires at least one projected row and durable results for every projected attempt.

Terminal executor_instance_id is derived only from projected effect-attempt authority: the one actual effect executor when all rows agree, or executor:multiple when they do not. A recovery process that only reconciles/finalizes is recorded separately as finalizer_kind ordinary-recovery plus its recovery-finalizer:* instance ID and can never replace executor_instance_id, create attempt authority, dispatch, or persist a new remote result. Inline finalization uses finalizer_kind effect-executor and a projected executor ID. Restore admission uses its exact finalizer sentinel and preserves the existing executor restore sentinels.

Terminal audit has an immediate composite foreign key (receipt_id,plan_id,claim_id) to the identically ordered unique consumption parent key; no receipt can attribute a terminal row to another plan or claim.
Every table has strict type, byte length, canonical timestamp, namespace, enum, foreign-key, and immutable update/delete guards.
legacyMigration: Insert legacy-untrusted authority-version rows for every pre-migration action plan; do not synthesize creator, approver, committer, presence, seal, or receipt fields.

New plans atomically insert trusted-v1 with reason trusted-create plus creator provenance. Existing rows receive legacy-untrusted with reason legacy-pre-authority. A missing marker or creator row is legacy-untrusted.

Legacy pending plans cannot approve or commit and return action.legacy_authority. Legacy executing plans may perform no new undispatched remote effect; already-dispatched attempts may only use existing read-only reconciliation and terminal attribution is marked legacy-untrusted.
Legacy terminal rows remain inspectable with provenanceStatus legacy-untrusted. They never become evidence for a new claim.
Drop no legacy rows during migration. Remove scope-only acceptance code in the same deployment; there is no feature flag, compatibility route, dual read, or lazy upgrade.
restoreAdmissionTransaction: After verified database replacement, take the exclusive authority file/process locks and before any listener, worker, recovery actor, session resolution, or challenge RPC starts, BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the restored database with one restore-event UUID/time.

Insert database-restore invalidations for every challenge with no consumption, expiry, or invalidation row and every approval with no consumption, expiry, cancellation, or invalidation row. Advance each distinct still-pending affected plan exactly once to version n+1 and regenerate its preview bindings, or expire it when its own expiry has arrived.
Do this regardless of matching authorityInstanceId, credential status, private-key availability, seal-key availability, or successful signature/seal verification.

For every restored action_plans row in executing state with a matching receipt/claim, preserve the receipt and claim rows, insert a terminal audit with state restore-quarantined, reason explicit-database-restore, the restore event ID, exact finalizer_kind restore-admission and finalizer_instance_id finalizer:restore-admission, deterministic result digest SHA-256(JSON.stringify(['action-restore-quarantine-v1',restoreEventId,planId,receiptId,claimId,restoredAt])), and executor disposition plus effect-authority count/digest derived only from durable attempt rows. Atomically clear the active claim pointer, set restore-quarantined, and advance version n to n+1.

Commit and assert zero available restored challenges/approvals and zero restored executing recovery candidates; any failure prevents service admission. Recovery queries categorically exclude restore-quarantined.

This covers backups made before later consume/cancel and backups made after consume but before dispatch whose original timeline later dispatched or completed. Restore can preserve audit and permit inspect only; it starts or resumes zero remote effects even when every old key remains present.

commonRules: All request and response objects are strict.
Path planId must equal body planId.

Approve and cancel bodies are transmitted once as exact bounded UTF-8 bytes. The broker challenge and final assertion bind SHA-256 of those raw bytes; the CLI must reuse the identical byte buffer without reserialization.
No request identity, profile, scope, presence, time, nonce, target digest, normalized intent, or seal fields are accepted.
Safe public provenance exposes principalId and profile, never credentialId, authEventId, ceremonyId, nonce, key ID, seal, or bearer material.

operatorSessionFlow: Before operator create or inspect, reuse an unexpired in-memory A1 non-approval session held by this CLI process; otherwise require attached TTY and request an open-session challenge for the exact fixed create/inspect scope pair.

Show the exact prompt 'Start a 10-minute operator session for action-plan create and inspect? [y/N]'. Only case-insensitive exact y or yes continues; EOF, non-TTY, timeout, empty/other input, structured mode, --yes/--force, environment, stdin, or saved answers create no challenge or session.

The fresh OS prompt is exactly 'Agent Mail START 10-minute CREATE and INSPECT session'. After signed challenge verification, receive the one-time session token over loopback response, retain it only in process memory, and send it only as Bearer authentication for create/inspect.

A session-expired/credential-expired/restarted daemon response causes one new interactive session ceremony, never silent fallback to an agent token or approval assertion. The session cannot invoke approve, cancel, commit, or any executor surface.
approveFlow: Obtain/reuse the exact A1 non-approval operator session, fetch inspect using its mail:action.inspect scope, and render the exact plan ID, version, action, every frozen target and MODSEQ, preview digest, normalized intent, plan expiry, and the 600-second maximum approval lifetime through the shared human-safe output context.
Require an attached TTY and prompt exactly: Approve this frozen action plan for one unattended commit within 10 minutes and no later than <planExpiresAt>? [y/N]
EOF, non-TTY, timeout, empty input, or any value other than a case-insensitive exact y or yes declines locally and sends no approve request.

After yes, serialize the strict approve body once, retain those exact raw bytes, request the owner-local A1 challenge with their base64url encoding, render the returned operatorDisplayCode, and obtain a fresh zero-reuse Secure Enclave signature whose OS prompt shows the same plan ID, full preview digest, and code.

Send the retained byte buffer unchanged with the AgentMail-Operator assertion. The authenticator and approval service, not the CLI request schema, supply and verify operator principal/profile/presence.
No --yes, --force, environment variable, stdin pipe, agent-unattended credential, saved prompt answer, or JSON identity field may bypass the prompt plus authentication ceremony.
Structured JSON mode may display an approval but cannot mint one; approval creation is human mode only. Commit remains non-interactive and requires agent-unattended authentication plus approvalId.
cancelFlow: Render the exact available approval, plan ID/version/preview digest, then prompt exactly: Cancel this one-use approval? [y/N]. The same fail-closed TTY and answer rules apply.

Serialize the strict cancellation body once, request a distinct cancel-approval challenge over exact DELETE/path/raw bytes, display its independently derived code, and require a fresh zero-reuse Secure Enclave signature with CANCEL in the OS reason.
Reuse of an approve ceremony for cancel, a cancel ceremony for approve, or any changed method/path/raw body rejects before cancellation.

chain: operator non-approval session challenge/consumption when used for create or inspect
authority instance and enrolled operator public credential
audit.durableJoin: planId -> creator and authority version -> approval -> challenge plus challenge-consumption signature proof -> one approval closure -> receipt and claim -> immutable attempt authority -> dispatch/result -> terminal effect-authority count/digest plus effect executor -> separately attributed non-authorizing finalizer
audit.reopenRule: A database reopen reconstructs the same actor IDs, profiles, bindings, closure, receipt, claim, attempts, and terminal result without consulting request logs or client state.

surfaceClosure.strictBoundary: Decode unknown request plus trusted authentication/request-binding object; reject extra identity or scope evidence.

surfaceClosure.entry: registered action route plus two-phase HTTP admission
surfaceClosure.strictBoundary: Exact method/path, capped assertion header, bounded streamed raw-body SHA-256, strict JSON, verified context.
CLI can request/sign a challenge and send the identical raw bytes; it has no storage/service import.
Accepts prepared service authority only; no string scope, public request, caller principal, or transient authorization ID shape.

Requires ordinary restart and an already consumed receipt plus matching claim/executing plan. Before all results are durable, any effect path still requires #202 fresh dispatch authority. After all results are durable, selection is finalization-only. Explicit-restore and restore-quarantined rows categorically reject.
surfaceClosure.postResultFinalizer: A distinct recovery-finalizer:* process identity may read/reconcile existing results and atomically finalize, but receives no adapter permission, creates no attempt authority/dispatch/result, and is stored separately from the projected effect executor.

requirements.text: No credential that can execute unattended mutation can mint the approval it consumes.

Creator, approver, committer, effect-executor, and recovery-finalizer provenance comes only from trusted authentication or internal process identity and remains durable without confusing finalization with mutation authority.
Approval is sealed over exact plan identity/version, preview, targets, intent, time, nonce, scope, and approver authority.
Approval consumption and plan claim are one atomic exactly-once closure under replay and concurrency.
Stale, changed, tampered, expired, cancelled, invalidated, scope-only, or legacy authority produces zero new remote effects.

Restart before or after consumption preserves authority state and existing partial/uncertain effect rules without reuse; recovery after durable results can reconcile/finalize but cannot perform another effect.
Audit reopen attributes creator through the complete effect-authority set, terminal result, and any distinct recovery finalizer without storing or exposing credential secrets.
Direct service, HTTP, CLI, storage, executor, and recovery surfaces share one strict authority and stable errors.
Every scope-only or ceremony-only representation is retired in one fail-closed migration with no alternate acceptance path.

decisions.decision: Adopt user-selected Policy A with a human-present operator approver and a distinct unattended agent committer.
Separate profiles by construction and additionally compare principal and credential IDs at consume.

Use user-selected A1: a macOS Secure Enclave P-256 key protected by Security.framework device-owner user presence, daemon challenge, native broker, and daemon public-key verification; a prompt alone is not authority.
Rename the domain act and public operation from authorize to approve; reserve authorization for generic access control.
Allow either accepted public profile to create; an operator uses only an A1-minted create/inspect session, and creation never implies approval.
Use exact canonical arrays, SHA-256 digests, and HMAC-SHA-256 under a separate daemon key to make database tampering detectable.
Limit approval to 600 seconds and to the earlier plan or credential expiry; reject at now >= expiry.
Persist immutable approval and constructive closure rows; never reopen a closed approval.
Consume, receipt, claim, and plan transition are one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.
Return stable 409 action.approval_consumed on every replay, including response-loss retry; inspect is the recovery path.
Cancellation requires the same operator principal with fresh presence and races atomically with consume.
Atomically advance each still-pending plan exactly once after approval expiry, cancellation, credential/key/config invalidation, or restore so replacement approval requires a regenerated preview.
Keep the executor internal and require receipt-linked attempt attribution before adapter permission.
Preserve consumed authority across partial and uncertain outcomes; reconciliation cannot reauthorize mutation.

Distinguish ordinary restart from explicit database restore: restart may retain current authority, but every restore invalidates live unconsumed authority and quarantines every restored consumed/executing plan before recovery even when every old key remains present.
Fail closed all legacy plans; never manufacture missing provenance or accept scope-only evidence.
Expose safe principal/profile attribution publicly while keeping credential and seal material internal.
Use one strict contract and one consume service for direct handler, HTTP, CLI, storage, and recovery composition.
Bind approve POST and cancellation DELETE independently to exact concrete paths and SHA-256 of the final raw bounded HTTP body bytes; ceremony uniqueness spans both operations.

Preserve authenticate-before-read admission with two-phase operator authentication: bounded assertion/challenge preflight before streaming, then strict body parse, raw digest comparison, signature verification, and atomic challenge consumption.

Seal every approval immutable field except the seal output itself exactly once, including user-presence time, exact request binding, key ID, and algorithm, using a machine-checked ordered field projection.
Mint a memory-only, at-most-600-second A1 operator session with exactly create and inspect scopes; it cannot approve, cancel, commit, or survive restart/configuration change.
Give every A1 operator credential an exact 365-day lifetime; equality is expired, expiry cannot be extended, and rotation/recovery creates a new lifetime.
Use the exact owner-only 32-byte approval seal keyring format and lifecycle; rotate active to verify-only, invalidate before removal, and categorically exclude it from backups and diagnostics.
Linearize approve/cancel/consume/session and outside-DB credential/key changes under one ordered file lock, process RW lock, revision/file recheck, and SQLite transaction protocol.
On explicit restore, convert every restored receipt-backed executing plan to terminal restore-quarantined before recovery; preserve audit but permit zero new remote effects.

Freeze deterministic strict storage semantics: closed authority-version reason pairs, all NOT NULL columns, constructive closure versions, and the receipt row's composite claim foreign key as the only link.

Authorize seal-key rotation and removal only with a daemon-issued one-use A1 administration challenge signed by the current Secure Enclave operator key and bound to exact operation, internal path, raw body, target, and expected keyring revision; same UID and a client prompt are transport/UX checks only.

Keep terminal effect attribution and recovery finalization distinct: derive the terminal executor only from the immutable receipt/claim attempt-authority set, commit that complete set by count and digest, and record a read-only recovery finalizer under a separate non-authorizing identity.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Policy B: operator approval atomically commits
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The user selected Policy A; B would remove the requested later unattended consume.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: One bearer with separate approve and commit scopes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Scope partition is ceremony-only when one credential can hold both.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Same principal with two credentials
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It does not satisfy the selected distinct unattended agent principal rule.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: TTY prompt or --yes as human-presence proof
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The daemon cannot independently verify a client-side ceremony.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Caller-supplied principal, profile, presence, issue time, expiry, scope, targets, or intent
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The acting caller could manufacture trusted authority fields.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Unsealed database approval row
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Database-field tampering would not be independently detectable.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Consume first and create the claim or receipt later
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Crash and concurrency windows could reuse approval or execute without durable attribution.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Idempotently return commit success on replay
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It obscures one-use consumption; inspect supplies recovery without authorizing another execution.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Reuse approval after partial, failure, cancellation, or uncertainty
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Some remote effect may already exist and authority is one-use, not outcome-conditioned.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Constructively backfill scope-only legacy rows
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Creator, approver, presence, binding, and consumption facts do not exist and cannot be inferred.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Back up approval HMAC secrets with the database
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It couples data recovery to secret recovery and makes a stolen backup sufficient to preserve live mutation authority.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Public executor token or endpoint
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It bypasses approval consumption and the existing executor isolation boundary.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: WebAuthn/FIDO2 A2 authenticator
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The user selected the macOS-native A1 mechanism; A2 adds RP/origin or CTAP provisioning and different portability/UX policy.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Software P-256 key, passphrase, static operator bearer, or prompt-only fallback when Secure Enclave/user presence is unavailable
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Any fallback would let unattended same-user software obtain or replay approval authority without independently verified device-owner presence.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Bind a canonical reserialization instead of the transmitted HTTP body bytes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It would leave the authenticated assertion detached from byte-level ingress; A1 binds the exact bounded bytes actually parsed.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Require a fresh Secure Enclave presence ceremony for every operator create and inspect request
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It is secure but adds avoidable friction; the exact short-lived non-approval session preserves separation without repeated prompts.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Give the A1 operator session approval or commit scope, or accept it as approval presence
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A reusable bearer would become ceremony or mutation authority and recreate self-authorization risk.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Treat explicit database restore like ordinary restart for consumed executing work
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A restored pre-dispatch snapshot can replay an effect already dispatched or completed on the original timeline.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Update credential/key files and approval rows under independent locks with eventual invalidation
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Consume could validate stale outside-DB authority after revocation/removal linearized and still return an executor capability.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Allow omitted/infinite operator credential expiry or regenerate a missing seal keyring for an existing database
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Both invent authority that cannot be derived from trusted durable state and therefore must fail closed.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Accept a same-UID bare seal-key rotate/remove discriminant after a client-side TTY or Security.framework prompt
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The daemon cannot verify that ceremony; any same-UID unattended process could rotate or remove verify-only keys and cause authority denial of service.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Write the recovery finalizer process into terminal executor_instance_id after crash-after-result
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It would relabel the actor that reconciled durable evidence as the actor authorized to perform the remote effect, destroying security-relevant executor attribution and hiding the immutable attempt authority.
